Take this free CAT Averages online test — 10 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and a worked explanation for every answer. The Averages chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Averages tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Averages

Simple average, weighted average, change in average when a member is added or removed, and average of special series.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Average = sum ÷ count; Sum = Average × Count.
  • Average of first n natural numbers = (n+1)/2.
  • Weighted average = Σ(wᵢxᵢ)/Σwᵢ.
  • If every value changes by k, the average changes by k.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Averaging two averages directly instead of weighting by counts.
  • Forgetting to use the total (sum) when a member changes.
  • Assuming the average is always a member of the set.

A batsman has an average of 45 after 10 innings. He scores 100 in the next innings. By how much does his average change?

faq.a: Only if the groups are equal in size. Otherwise use the weighted average (weight each by its count).

faq.q: How does adding a person change the average?
faq.a: New average = old average + (new value − old average)/(new count).
